title: calculate_standings MCP tool returns protocol error -32602 on every call
evidence: src/server.ts:8-13 result() sets structuredContent = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(data)); src/server.ts:110-117 calculate_standings passes data = service.standings(...).slice(0, limit), a StandingRow[] (array). CallToolResultSchema in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0 (dist/esm/types.js:1472 structuredContent: z.object({}).loose()) validates on the client and rejects arrays. Reproduced via InMemoryTransport client.callTool('calculate_standings',{season:2019}) -> MCP error -32602 'Invalid tools/call result: expected record, received array'. Root computation is correct (service.standings(2019) -> 20 rows, leader Flamengo-RJ 90 pts) and IS reachable via competition_summary (returns fine, standings[] included), so the requirement's compute-not-hardcoded criterion is met, but the dedicated standings tool is unusable.
suggestion: Wrap the array before returning, e.g. result(formatStandings(data), { season, competition, standings: data }) so structuredContent is an object. Same latent risk exists only where data is an array; all other tools return objects and pass.

title: Factual gate scored 0.0 — 2019 Serie A standings unretrievable, downstream of the R9 tool bug
evidence: _factual.json: {"ok": false, "score": 0.0, "note": "no tool returned a 2019 Serie A table naming Flamengo (tried 4 candidate tools)"}. The probe's most direct tool (calculate_standings) errors -32602 on every call; competition_summary reports champion as 'Flamengo-RJ' (state suffix retained) rather than 'Flamengo'.
suggestion: Fix calculate_standings (see R9) and/or expose a de-suffixed team name so the standard standings query resolves the champion.
